Evidence Note 01/30

European buyers do not decide on your operation. They decide on your evidence.

The operation may be excellent. If the file that describes it is scattered across e-mails, spreadsheets and three departments, the procurement committee sees a gap, not a supplier.

Over the next 30 days this page publishes one note per morning on EU–Brazil supplier evidence: CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD, contract clauses, board files. Each note separates fact from interpretation. No sustainability slogans.

One working definition to start:
Supplier evidence = the set of records a buyer can act on without calling you.

If a buyer has to call you to understand your file, the file is not finished.

#SupplierEvidence #Procurement #SupplyChainRisk

You received a request from a European buyer. A questionnaire, a clause, a data request. With a deadline.

Before you answer it, you need to know what your file can already defend — and where it cannot.

That is what the scope assessment does:
• you send the request you received;
• we read it against your existing records, in Portuguese, at origin;
• you get a written view of what is defensible, what is missing and what should be answered first.

First reply within one business day. A written proposal only if a full review is worth your money.

Send the request here: https://www.villanovaesg.com/supplier-evidence-risk-intake/

Advisory review — not an audit, certification or legal opinion.

#SupplierEvidence #Exporters #CFO

Evidence Note 02/30

The law is European. The request lands in a Brazilian inbox.

This is the structural problem of EU–Brazil supply chains. CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD and CSRD impose obligations on the EU company. The EU company discharges those obligations by asking its suppliers for evidence.

So the Brazilian exporter is rarely "in scope". It is in the chain of activities of someone who is.

Practical consequence:
• you will not be fined by Brussels;
• you can be repriced, delisted or replaced by Munich, Rotterdam or Milan.

The enforcement mechanism for a non-EU supplier is the purchase order, not the regulator.

Fact: obligations sit with EU operators and importers.
Interpretation: procurement will keep passing the evidence burden upstream, regardless of simplification packages.

#SupplierEvidence #Procurement #DueDiligence

Seu comprador europeu não vai esperar a lei entrar em vigor para pedir evidência. Ele já está pedindo.

Questionário de renovação, cláusula nova no contrato, pedido de dados de emissões, prova de origem do lote. Tudo com prazo.

A Villanova ESG revisa o seu arquivo de evidências na origem, em português, contra o pedido real que você recebeu:
• o que já é defensável;
• o que está faltando;
• o que responder primeiro.

Sem lista de preços. Avaliação de escopo primeiro; proposta escrita só se a revisão valer o seu dinheiro.

Envie o pedido do comprador: https://www.villanovaesg.com/solicitar-analise/

Evidence Note 03/30

Five levels. One question: can a buyer act on your file without calling you?

The Supplier Evidence Maturity Model (SEMM) grades a supplier evidence file from 0 to 4:

0 Absent — no file exists.
1 Reactive — every request becomes a project.
2 Organised — records exist, gaps unknown.
3 Decision-ready — a buyer can act on the file.
4 Continuously managed — the next request is an export, not an emergency.

Most Brazilian exporters we see sit at 1 or 2. The operation is real. The evidence is not yet usable by someone else.

The jump that puts revenue on the table is 2 → 3. That is where a renewal stops being a negotiation about trust and becomes a review of documents.

The model is public and citable: https://www.villanovaesg.com/supplier-evidence-maturity-model/

#SupplierEvidence #SEMM #Procurement

This morning's note: most exporter files sit at SEMM level 1 or 2. The buyer needs level 3.

The Supplier Evidence Review is the engagement that closes that gap.

What you get:
• gap register — every missing or weak record, against the buyer's actual request;
• prioritised plan — what to fix first, who owns it, by when;
• board-readable file — one document your CFO can defend in a renewal.

From a 30-day diagnostic to a full review, scoped case by case on the shape of your operation.

Start here: https://www.villanovaesg.com/supplier-evidence-file-assessment/

Advisory review — not an audit or certification.

#SupplierEvidence #CFO #SupplyChainRisk

Evidence Note 04/30

"Our operation is fine." Usually true. Also irrelevant.

The pattern repeats in steel, coffee, leather, soy:
• the environmental licence exists — in the legal department;
• the production data exists — in a spreadsheet nobody versions;
• the origin records exist — with the cooperative, on paper;
• the contract clause exists — signed, never read against the file.

Four real facts. Zero usable evidence. Because evidence is not the existence of a record. It is the ability of a third party to locate it, read it and rely on it.

When a procurement analyst in Europe opens your answer, three things decide the outcome:
1. Is each claim tied to a document?
2. Is each document dated, owned and current?
3. Does the whole thing fit in one file?

Miss one and the committee marks "evidence insufficient". Not "supplier bad". Insufficient. And insufficient reprices.

#SupplierEvidence #Traceability #Procurement

Licença no jurídico. Dados de produção numa planilha. Origem no papel da cooperativa. Cláusula assinada e nunca lida contra o arquivo.

A operação está certa. A evidência está espalhada. É isso que o comprador europeu vê.

A revisão de evidências para exportadores organiza o que já existe no formato que o comprador consegue usar:
• registro de lacunas contra o pedido real (EUDR, CBAM, CSDDD, questionário);
• plano priorizado com responsável e prazo;
• arquivo único, legível pelo CFO e pelo comitê de compras.

Detalhes: https://www.villanovaesg.com/revisao-evidencias-eudr-cbam-csddd-exportadores/

Escopo definido caso a caso. Trabalho consultivo, não certificação.

#SupplierEvidence #Rastreabilidade #Exportadores

Evidence Note 05/30

"Complete this questionnaire before we renew."

This sentence costs more than any fine. Here is why.

A renewal questionnaire is not a compliance exercise. It is a scoring exercise. The buyer's procurement team scores suppliers and the score feeds two decisions: volume allocation and price negotiation.

A weak answer does not get you rejected. It gets you:
• a lower share of next year's volume;
• a "risk premium" discussed at the price table;
• a request for an audit you pay for.

The damage happens before anyone says the word "non-compliant".

Three questions to ask about your last questionnaire:
1. Who answered it — sales or the people who hold the records?
2. How many answers were "yes" without an attached document?
3. Did anyone read the renewal contract clauses against those answers?

If the third answer is no, the next note is for you.

#SupplierEvidence #Procurement #ContractRisk

The questionnaire was answered "yes". The contract says "supplier shall provide evidence upon request". Nobody checked whether the two match.

The Contract Clause Risk Review reads your EU-facing supply agreement clause by clause and answers one question per clause: what can you actually prove today?

Output:
• clause-by-clause map of evidence obligations (due diligence, CBAM data, origin, audit rights, termination triggers);
• what your file supports, what it does not;
• what to fix before signing — or before the buyer asks.

Details: https://www.villanovaesg.com/contract-clause-risk-review-eu-facing-suppliers/

Advisory review. Not legal advice — your counsel keeps the pen; we give them the evidence picture.

#SupplierEvidence #ContractRisk #CFO

Evidence Note 06/30

Every claim in a supplier file should carry a label: Fact, Interpretation or Hypothesis.

This is the discipline we apply to our own reports and it is the single cheapest upgrade to any evidence file.

Fact — a document, dated and sourced, says it. "Licence no. X valid until Y."
Interpretation — a reasonable reading of facts. "The buyer's clause likely refers to EUDR Article 9 information."
Hypothesis — something we believe but cannot yet document. "Our tier-2 supplier is probably outside the EUDR scope."

Why it matters commercially:
• buyers trust files that admit what they do not know;
• auditors stop at the first unlabelled claim;
• boards cannot approve a risk they cannot classify.

A file that is 60% fact, honestly labelled, beats a file made entirely of assertions.

#SupplierEvidence #Compliance #Boardroom

Pergunta para o CFO exportador: do que você respondeu ao último questionário europeu, quanto era fato documentado e quanto era afirmação?

Se a resposta é "não sei", a revisão começa por aí.

O que fazemos na avaliação de escopo:

• classificamos cada resposta sua em fato, interpretação ou hipótese;
• apontamos onde a afirmação sem documento vira risco de preço, de volume ou de contrato.

Resposta em um dia útil. Proposta escrita só se a revisão completa fizer sentido.

Evidence Note 08/30 — CBAM week

Since 1 January 2026, CBAM is in its definitive period. Translation for a Brazilian exporter: the embedded-emissions number of your product now has a price attached on the importer's side.

During the transitional period (2023–2025) the importer reported. Now the importer pays for certificates based on the declared embedded emissions of what it imports.

Where does the number come from? From you — or from a default value.

Fact: CBAM covers, among others, iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity, including a range of downstream goods.
Fact: the financial obligation sits with the EU importer.
Interpretation: an importer that pays on your number will negotiate your price on your number.

This week: what the data request looks like, why default values are a price problem, and who in your company should own the figure.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #CarbonExposure

Exporta aço, alumínio, cimento ou fertilizante para a União Europeia? Desde janeiro de 2026 o importador paga certificado CBAM com base nas emissões incorporadas do que ele compra de você.

Se você não fornece o dado, ele usa um valor padrão. E negocia preço em cima dele.

A revisão de evidências CBAM organiza o seu número:
• fontes de dados por instalação e rota de produção;
• metodologia e responsáveis;
• lacunas que fazem o importador cair no valor padrão.

Detalhes: https://www.villanovaesg.com/revisao-evidencias-eudr-cbam-csddd-exportadores/

Trabalho consultivo. Não é verificação acreditada nem parecer aduaneiro.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #Exportadores

Evidence Note 09/30 — CBAM

The default value is not a technical fallback. It is a commercial penalty you pay without seeing the invoice.

When an exporter cannot supply verifiable embedded-emissions data, the importer's declaration falls back on default values. Default values are designed to be conservative. Conservative means high. High means more certificates. More certificates means a higher landed cost of your product.

The importer does not absorb that cost. It shows up as:
• a price-reduction request at renewal;
• a comparison against a competitor who did supply data;
• a reallocation of volume.

So the first CBAM question for a Brazilian CFO is not "are we compliant?". It is: "what is the gap between our actual embedded emissions and the default value the importer would otherwise use — and who is paying for that gap today?"

If nobody in the company can answer that in one sentence, the number is not under control.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #CFO

Evidence Note 10/30 — CBAM

What a CBAM data request actually asks a Brazilian producer for. Not the regulation — the e-mail.

Typical structure:
1. Installation identification — which plant produced the goods.
2. Production route — e.g. blast furnace vs. electric arc furnace; primary vs. secondary aluminium.
3. Direct emissions — fuels and process emissions attributable to the goods.
4. Indirect emissions — electricity consumed, with the emission factor used.
5. Precursors — embedded emissions of inputs already covered.
6. Methodology and monitoring — how the figures were obtained, by whom, for which period.
7. Verification status — whether any third party has reviewed the data.

Most Brazilian files answer 1 and 2 immediately, 3 and 4 after internal negotiation, and 5–7 not at all.

Items 5–7 are where the importer decides whether your number is usable or whether the default value applies.

Fact: the categories above reflect the CBAM reporting structure. Interpretation: buyers will keep asking for 6 and 7 even when not strictly required, because it de-risks their own declaration.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #Traceability

Sete blocos num pedido de dados CBAM. A maioria dos exportadores brasileiros responde os dois primeiros e trava no quinto.

Precursores, metodologia, verificação: é aí que o importador decide se usa o seu número ou o valor padrão.

Evidence Note 11/30 — CBAM

CBAM is a cost on the European side. That makes it a procurement lever on the Brazilian side.

Two exporters, same product, same port:
• Exporter A supplies installation-level emissions data with a documented methodology.
• Exporter B supplies a letter saying "we are committed to sustainability".

The importer's CBAM cost on A is calculated. On B it is defaulted. The spread between the two is real money, every quarter, for as long as the contract runs.

Procurement will see that spread. The question is only whether you see it first.

Three uses of the same data file:
1. defend price at renewal;
2. qualify for buyers who have decided to source only from "data-ready" suppliers;
3. feed your own Scope 1 and 2 figures without a second project.

One file. Three commercial outcomes. That is why CBAM evidence belongs to the CFO, not to the sustainability team alone.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #Procurement

Exporter A has installation-level data. Exporter B has a sustainability letter. Same product, different landed cost in Europe.

The CBAM Evidence Review puts you on the A side of that comparison with what you already have — production records, energy bills, process data — organised into a file the importer can rely on.

Scoped case by case: one installation or several, one product line or the full CBAM-covered range.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #CFO

Evidence Note 12/30 — CBAM

Who owns the number? In most Brazilian producers we review, the honest answer is "nobody".

Environmental has the licence. Production has the process data. Finance has the energy invoices. Sales talks to the importer. Each holds a piece. No one holds the figure the importer declares.

The result is predictable: the data request arrives, four departments reply with four spreadsheets, and the importer's declarant picks the default value because reconciling them is not his job.

Minimum governance for a CBAM-ready file:
• one named owner of the embedded-emissions figure (usually controlling or finance);
• one monitoring methodology document, versioned;
• one period convention aligned with the importer's declaration calendar;
• one place where the supporting records live.

None of this requires new software. It requires a decision about ownership. That decision is a board-level decision, because the exposure is commercial.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #Boardroom

Quem é o dono do número de emissões incorporadas na sua empresa?

Se a resposta demora mais de cinco segundos, o importador europeu já está usando o valor padrão — e negociando preço em cima dele.

A revisão de evidências define:
• dono do número;
• metodologia documentada e versionada;
• período alinhado ao calendário de declaração do importador;
• onde ficam os registros de suporte.

Sem software novo. Com decisão de governança e um arquivo que o declarante CBAM do comprador consegue usar.

Detalhes: https://www.villanovaesg.com/revisao-evidencias-eudr-cbam-csddd-exportadores/

Trabalho consultivo, não verificação.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #CFO

Evidence Note 13/30 — CBAM

A note on Scope 1 and 2 reporting versus CBAM embedded emissions. They are related. They are not the same number.

Corporate Scope 1 and 2 (GHG Protocol logic) describe the company's total emissions for a period.
CBAM embedded emissions describe the emissions attributable to a specific quantity of a specific good from a specific installation.

Common error: an exporter sends its corporate GHG inventory in reply to a CBAM data request. The importer cannot use it. The default value applies.

What the importer needs is an allocation: total installation emissions → production route → tonne of product. With precursors handled separately.

Fact: CBAM uses its own methodology, defined in the implementing rules.
Interpretation: a producer that already runs a GHG inventory is 60–70% of the way there; the missing 30–40% is allocation and documentation, not measurement.

If you have an inventory and no allocation, you have data and no evidence.

#SupplierEvidence #CBAM #Scope3

You already have a GHG inventory. Your importer still asked for CBAM data. Those are different numbers — and the gap between them is allocation and documentation, not measurement.

Send us the data request your importer actually sent. In one business day you get a written view of:
• whether your existing inventory can be allocated to the goods in question;
• what documentation is missing for the importer's declarant;
• whether a full CBAM Evidence Review is worth your money.

Scope assessment first. Proposal only if justified.

Evidence Note 14/30 — weekend read, CBAM

A five-point readiness check for Brazilian exporters of CBAM goods. Score yourself honestly.

1. Installation-level data — can you produce direct and indirect emissions per plant, per production route, for a defined period? (yes / partially / no)
2. Allocation — can you express that as embedded emissions per tonne of the exported good? (yes / partially / no)
3. Precursors — do you know the embedded emissions of your covered inputs, or at least which ones are covered? (yes / partially / no)
4. Methodology document — is there a written, versioned description of how the figures are obtained? (yes / no)
5. Owner — is one person accountable for the figure the importer declares? (yes / no)

Five yes: your file is a commercial asset. Discuss price with confidence.
Three or fewer: the importer is probably on default values. The spread is coming out of your margin, quietly.

Evidence Note 15/30 — EUDR week

45 days to 30 December 2026.

That is the EUDR application date for large and medium-sized operators and traders. Micro and small enterprises follow on 30 June 2027. The Commission has stated it will not reopen the core text.

For a Brazilian exporter of coffee, cocoa, soy, cattle products, leather, wood, rubber or palm-oil derivatives, the practical meaning:
• your EU buyer must file a due diligence statement before placing your product on the EU market;
• that statement rests on data about origin, geolocation and legality that only you can supply;
• buyers are not waiting for 30 December — the requests have been arriving all year.

Fact: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended; application 30 Dec 2026 (large/medium) and 30 Jun 2027 (micro/small).
Interpretation: the supplier that delivers a clean EUDR data package in Q4 2026 becomes the buyer's path of least resistance in Q1 2027.

This week: what the data package contains, where Brazilian files usually break, and who holds the obligation versus who holds the evidence.

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #Traceability

"Prove origin and geolocation for every shipment."

That request, in some form, is already in the inbox of most Brazilian exporters of coffee, soy, beef, leather, wood and rubber. From 30 December 2026 it becomes the condition for entering the EU market.

The EUDR Evidence Readiness Review maps what you have against what the buyer's due diligence statement needs:
• origin and plot geolocation — format, completeness, chain of custody;
• legality of production — which documents, for which plots, for which period;
• gap register and prioritised plan, by supplier tier.

Details: https://www.villanovaesg.com/eudr-evidence-readiness-review/

Advisory review — not a due diligence statement, not certification.

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #Exporters

Evidence Note 16/30 — EUDR

The EUDR obligation belongs to the EU operator. The EUDR evidence belongs to you. That asymmetry defines the next six months.

What the EU operator must do: exercise due diligence, collect information, assess risk, mitigate it, and file a due diligence statement in the EU information system before placing the product on the market.

What the operator cannot do without you: identify the plots, confirm production dates against the 31 December 2020 cut-off, document legality under Brazilian law.

So the operator will ask. And since the operator carries the penalty, the operator will ask for more than the minimum.

Expect requests for:
• geolocation of every plot of land (point for small plots, polygon above the size threshold);
• harvest / production period;
• chain-of-custody records from plot to export lot;
• legality documents — land tenure, environmental, labour — with a Brazilian legal basis the buyer can read.

Interpretation: buyers will consolidate suppliers around those who can deliver this package without a project each time. That is a volume decision, not a compliance decision.

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #DueDiligence

Café, cacau, soja, carne, couro, madeira, borracha. Se você exporta para a UE, o seu comprador precisa de uma declaração de due diligence a partir de 30 de dezembro de 2026 — e os dados que sustentam essa declaração estão com você.

Geolocalização dos talhões. Período de produção. Cadeia de custódia do talhão ao lote. Documentos de legalidade com base legal brasileira legível para o comprador.

A revisão de evidências EUDR organiza esse pacote a partir do que já existe na sua operação e na sua base de fornecedores:
• registro de lacunas por fornecedor e por talhão;
• plano priorizado;
• arquivo que o comprador consegue usar na própria declaração.

Detalhes: https://www.villanovaesg.com/revisao-evidencias-eudr-cbam-csddd-exportadores/

Trabalho consultivo. Não emitimos declaração de due diligence nem certificação.

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #Exportadores

Evidence Note 18/30 — EUDR

Deforestation-free is half the test. Legally produced is the other half — and it is the half Brazilian files usually skip.

The EUDR requires that relevant products be both:
(a) deforestation-free — no production on land deforested after 31 December 2020; and
(b) produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production.

(b) is broad. The regulation's own list of relevant legislation covers, among others: land use rights, environmental protection, forest-related rules, third parties' rights, labour rights, human rights protected under international law, free prior and informed consent where applicable, tax, anti-corruption, trade and customs.

So the EU operator will ask, for each plot or supplier: what documents show that production complied with Brazilian law on those points?

Most files answer with a CAR number and an environmental licence. That covers a fraction of (b).

Interpretation: buyers will not ask for a legal opinion per plot. They will ask for a structured legality file — which documents, for which obligations, with dates — that lets their own risk assessment conclude "negligible risk". The supplier that provides the structure removes the buyer's hardest step.

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #DueDiligence

"Livre de desmatamento" é metade do teste EUDR. "Produzido conforme a legislação brasileira" é a outra metade — direito de uso da terra, ambiental, trabalhista, tributário, anticorrupção, entre outros.

CAR e licença ambiental cobrem uma fração disso.

Se o seu comprador europeu enviou um pedido de informação EUDR, mande o pedido real para a avaliação de escopo. Em um dia útil:
• o que o seu arquivo de legalidade já cobre;
• o que falta por obrigação e por fornecedor;
• se uma revisão completa faz sentido antes de 30 de dezembro.

https://www.villanovaesg.com/solicitar-analise/

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #RiscoRegulatório

Evidence Note 19/30 — EUDR

The due diligence statement is one form. The file behind it is the product.

When the EU operator files the DDS in the information system, it declares that due diligence was exercised and that risk is negligible. The authorities can then ask for the underlying documentation.

That documentation is where your evidence ends up. Not in the form — in the file the operator must keep for five years.

Consequence for the supplier:
• a sloppy data package does not fail at filing; it fails at inspection, months later, with your buyer's name on it;
• the buyer knows this, which is why requests go beyond the minimum;
• after a first inspection round, buyers will tighten supplier requirements, not loosen them.

Fact: operators must keep DDS-related information for five years; competent authorities can request it.
Interpretation: the suppliers that stay are those whose packages survive the operator's own internal audit before the external one.

Design your EUDR file for the inspection, not for the form.

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #Compliance

Evidence Note 20/30 — EUDR

"We are small, so 30 June 2027 applies to us." Probably not the date that matters.

The later date applies to micro and small enterprises as EU operators or traders. Your buyer — the importer, roaster, tannery, trading house — is in most cases a large or medium enterprise. Its date is 30 December 2026.

Your size in Brazil does not change your buyer's date in Europe. And your buyer's date is the one that decides when your product stops moving.

Two further points often misread:
• products already covered by the EU Timber Regulation follow the earlier date even for small operators;
• simplified declarations for micro and small primary operators in low-risk countries do not remove the information the buyer needs from you.

Fact: 30 Dec 2026 (large/medium), 30 Jun 2027 (micro/small, with exceptions).
Interpretation: for a Brazilian supplier, the operative date is always the buyer's date.

#SupplierEvidence #EUDR #Procurement

"Somos pequenos, então o prazo é junho de 2027."

O prazo que importa é o do seu comprador. Importador, torrefador, curtume, trading: grandes e médios, data de 30 de dezembro de 2026.

O tamanho da sua empresa no Brasil não muda a data do comprador na Europa.

A revisão de evidências EUDR para exportadores organiza, com base no que já existe:
• geolocalização por talhão e por lote;
• período de produção;

Evidence Note 21/30 — weekend read, EUDR

The structure of an EUDR supplier file that a buyer can use. Six folders. No software required.

1. Supplier register — every farm, cooperative or intermediary in the chain, with role and tier.
2. Plot geolocation — one entry per plot, point or polygon, source and date of the coordinate.
3. Production periods — harvest / slaughter / felling dates per plot, tied to the cut-off date.
4. Chain of custody — the link from plot → intermediary → processing → export lot, with the documents at each hand-over.
5. Legality file — per obligation category (land, environmental, labour, tax, others): which document, which issuer, which validity.
6. Open items — what is missing, who owns it, by when. Labelled fact / interpretation / hypothesis.

A buyer who receives these six folders can run its own risk assessment in days instead of weeks. That buyer will come back.

Evidence Note 22/30 — CSDDD week

After the Omnibus, the CSDDD applies to EU companies with more than 5,000 employees and over EUR 1.5 billion net worldwide turnover, from 26 July 2029. Fewer companies, later date.

The conclusion many Brazilian exporters drew: "this no longer concerns us."

That is the wrong reading, for three reasons.

1. The companies that remain in scope are precisely the large buyers that anchor most EU–Brazil trade in steel, agri-commodities, leather and textiles.
2. Due diligence under the CSDDD still extends through the chain of activities to business partners. Large buyers discharge it contractually — with you.
3. Buyers did not wait for 2029. The clauses are already in supply agreements signed in 2025 and 2026.

Fact: Directive (EU) 2026/470 — thresholds 5,000 employees / EUR 1.5 bn; transposition by 26 July 2028; application 26 July 2029; EU-level civil liability regime removed, national law remains.
Interpretation: scope narrowed the number of obligated companies, not the evidence demand on their suppliers.

This week: what those clauses actually ask for, the CSRD value-chain cap, and what a board should see.

Evidence Note 23/30 — CSDDD

The contract moved before the law did. Read your supply agreement; the CSDDD is already in it.

Typical clause language appearing in EU–Brazil supply agreements since 2024:
• "Supplier shall comply with Buyer's Supplier Code of Conduct and provide evidence of compliance upon request."
• "Supplier shall cooperate with Buyer's human rights and environmental due diligence, including by providing information on its own suppliers."
• "Buyer may audit Supplier's facilities and records, at Supplier's cost in case of non-conformity."
• "Buyer may suspend or terminate in case of material breach of the above."

None of these clauses mentions the CSDDD. All of them implement it.

What the supplier usually does: signs, files the contract, moves on.
What the supplier should do: for each evidence obligation, write down what document would satisfy it today. Where the answer is "none", that is a termination trigger waiting for a bad quarter.

Interpretation: as the CSDDD moves towards 2029, these clauses get more specific, not less. The cost of answering them rises with each renewal cycle.

Evidence Note 24/30 — CSRD

The Omnibus introduced a value-chain cap. Suppliers should understand it — and not over-read it.

What it says: companies reporting under the CSRD may not request from value-chain partners with fewer than 1,000 employees more information than the voluntary standard for SMEs (VSME) contains. The cap cannot be overridden by contract.

What suppliers hear: "they cannot ask us for much anymore."

What it actually means:
• the cap limits CSRD-driven requests only; CBAM, EUDR and contractual due diligence requests are untouched;
• the cap defines a ceiling, and that ceiling — the VSME — is a full structured dataset, not a one-page letter;
• large buyers will standardise their supplier questionnaires on the VSME structure, because that is the maximum they can ask for.

Fact: Directive (EU) 2026/470 — CSRD scope above 1,000 employees and EUR 450 million; value-chain cap tied to the VSME standard.
Interpretation: the VSME becomes the de facto template for supplier ESG data requests from large EU buyers. A supplier whose file is organised along those lines answers once and reuses.

Evidence Note 25/30 — contract clauses

Anatomy of one clause. "Supplier shall provide evidence of compliance with applicable environmental and social requirements upon Buyer's reasonable request."

Fourteen words that hide five questions. Answer them before you sign.

1. "Evidence" — documents? declarations? third-party reports? The clause does not say. Your file should define it: for each requirement, the document that satisfies it.
2. "Applicable requirements" — Brazilian law? the buyer's code? EU regulations the buyer is subject to? Usually all three. List them.
3. "Upon request" — within what time? A clause with no deadline is read by procurement as "immediately".
4. "Reasonable" — reasonable for whom? Without a definition, the buyer's compliance team decides.
5. Consequence — read the termination and audit clauses together with this one. That is where the money is.

Interpretation: suppliers lose less by negotiating definitions into these clauses than by negotiating price. A defined evidence obligation is one you can plan and cost. An undefined one is a liability with no number.

Evidence Note 26/30 — CSDDD

The EU-wide civil liability regime was removed from the CSDDD. Buyers reacted by tightening contracts, not loosening them.

Why: liability under national law remains. Administrative penalties remain — capped, but material. And reputational exposure never had a statutory basis to begin with.

A large EU buyer therefore still needs to show, to its own board and supervisory authority, that it identified, prioritised and addressed risks in its chain of activities. The cheapest way to show that is a documented supplier base.

So the supplier sees:
• more detailed questionnaires;
• contractual rights to information about tier-2 and tier-3;
• supplier "risk ratings" that drive sourcing decisions internally and are never shared with the supplier.

You will not be told your rating. You will see it in the volume you get.

Fact: Directive (EU) 2026/470 removed the harmonised EU civil liability provision; national regimes and administrative penalties remain.
Interpretation: the supplier's exposure moved from a theoretical lawsuit to a very practical procurement score.

Evidence Note 27/30 — the board file

What a Brazilian board should see about EU supplier evidence. One page. Four blocks.

1. Exposure — share of revenue from EU buyers; which of those buyers are subject to CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD or CSRD; which contracts carry evidence clauses with termination rights.
2. Status — SEMM level per buyer relationship (0–4); number of open evidence requests and their age; number of "yes without document" answers in the last questionnaire cycle.
3. Gap — the five records whose absence most directly threatens volume or price, with owner and date.
4. Decision — what the board is asked to approve: ownership of the file, budget, deadline.

What the board should not see: a sustainability narrative, a list of certifications in progress, a slide about commitment.

The board's question is not "are we sustainable?". It is "can we lose a buyer we cannot afford to lose, and what does it cost to prevent that?"

A board that can answer that in one page is a board that can defend the P&L.

Evidence Note 29/30 — Scope 3

Your emissions are your buyer's Scope 3. That sentence explains most of the data requests you receive that are not labelled CBAM.

A large EU company reporting under the CSRD, or managing its own climate targets, needs purchased-goods emissions. Brazilian suppliers are a material line in that calculation for steel, agri-commodities, leather, pulp and textiles.

Two ways the buyer gets that number:
• spend-based estimate — an industry average multiplied by what it paid you. Conservative. High. Not your number.
• supplier-specific data — your actual figure, allocated to what the buyer bought.

The spend-based path is the default. It overstates most Brazilian producers and makes you look worse than a European competitor with the same process.

Interpretation: a supplier that provides allocated, documented, periodised emissions data moves from "industry average" to "known quantity" in the buyer's model. Known quantities are harder to replace.

Fact: the same installation data that feeds CBAM feeds the buyer's Scope 3. One dataset, maintained once.
